card.name: Linking words in old narrative prose
card.fires_on: Short linking words (to, of, with, in, be) and some verbs or adjectives inside long sentences of older-style historical or travel prose. The marked word usually comes right before a phrase that completes the clause.

modes.label: Prepositions mid-clause
modes.description: A small preposition or infinitive 'to' in the middle of a long, old-fashioned sentence.
modes.example: required by law to attend military exercises on certain days only, but at other times left<< to>> pursue their usual occupations.

modes.label: Descriptive word in an idiom
modes.description: An adjective or verb in a fixed phrase in a narrative passage.
modes.example: he "often painted the difficulties in the<< worst>> colours"

card.plain: It fires on small connecting words in long, old-fashioned storytelling sentences, not on any medical content.
